## Human participation and selection

The human requested AI-generated philosophical essays, supplied or retrieved primary texts, set resource and length constraints, asked for stronger arguments and literature checks, and arranged comparisons between model outputs. The recorded workflow instructions also requested adversarial review and subsequent revision. The human stated that philosophical feedback was being withheld for the contest. The available record does not replace a complete audit of every earlier exchange.

The inspected corpus contains ten developed manuscript tracks and eight exploratory drafts. Three developed OpenAI manuscripts rework the three original Claude projects; the tracks are therefore not all independent topics. The project also generated a 120-card idea register, narrowed through 40, 16, and eight candidates, and a separate six-problem ambitious-track selection. These counts measure candidates and artifacts, not established discoveries. Revisions, blind-review copies, and a later A6 research note are not counted as additional essays.

The present preparation set is provisional. A current-version referee result could change which manuscripts are selected. No contest entry was submitted during this revision pass.

## Sources, evaluation, and tools

The authoring workflows used supplied documents, repository source extracts, and web retrieval for literature comparison and citation checks. The argument-agnostic scaffold required explicit claims, strong objections, source fidelity, and a distinction between novelty and correctness. The project used synthetic AI referee perspectives. These are not reviews endorsed by the philosophers whose research informed a perspective.

Validation distinguishes hand proofs, exact examples, finite enumeration, numerical checks, and source-reading boundaries. This revised manuscript counts 5,600 words under the repository strict counter, excluding its reference section and including title, headings, abstract, mathematical tokens, and footnotes. Its basic manuscript scan returned no hard flags. These checks do not establish originality, philosophical importance, or completeness of citation verification.

An OpenAI assistant revised E2 v4 against Gallow's author-hosted full text and the repository manuscript.
